request.summary: Find why Task Session readiness enforcement is causing repeated repair turns and propose bounded changes.
request.intent: Complete Inventory-first maintenance reflection without canonical mutation.

execution.notes: Inventory lookup selected five relevant entries. Reflection proposed one additive Task Session diagnostic change, routed the primary Invoke change to Spellcraft, and stopped because approved_change_scope is absent.

anti_pattern_hits: reusable maintenance validation reports pass while example Quality Bar and Anti-Pattern criteria remain unchecked

workflow_gaps.summary: The Sigil Maintenance Loop harness does not fail or justify empty Quality Bar and Anti-Pattern criteria.
workflow_gaps.evidence: All four example outputs reported QUALITY_BAR_STATUS=not_checked and zero criteria while the harness returned VALIDATION=pass.

useful_patterns: Inventory remained a read-only non-authority input
canonical mutation stopped without explicit approved change scope
cross-owner repairs were separated into Sigil Development, Spellcraft, and Invoke Refresh routes
observer.recommendation: Approve at most one exact owner scope; do not bundle Task Session diagnostics with Invoke producer repair.

rejected_changes: treat Dispatch Spec pass as execution readiness
copy producer validators into Task Session
maintenance.next_reflection_trigger: after one repaired intent-route package WPRA v2 result or three additional owner-routed diagnostic failures
